summary: Toronto picks a mayor today, Trump says the trade war with Canada will end "pretty soon," and a rate decision and an EU summit come later this week.
body: Toronto votes today, Monday, Oct. 26; polls are open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. [^4]. Mayor Olivia Chow and former councillor Brad Bradford ended the campaign in what polls for CP24 and CTV call a statistical tie, with Bradford about three points behind [^4]. The clearest difference is on taxes: Chow says she will keep property tax rises near inflation, while Bradford promises a one-year freeze and to remove the land transfer tax on the first $1.1 million of a home's price [^4]. Results come in tonight, after this brief was written.

On trade, Trump told a rally in Michigan on Sunday that the dispute with Canada would end "pretty soon" and that Canada was "willing to give us anything," The Canadian Press reports; the Prime Minister's Office did not immediately reply [^1]. Canada left formal talks in August, and 50% US tariffs and Canadian counter-tariffs are in force; Trump said Friday he would lift some tariffs at month's end while adding others [^1]. Separately, the US Embassy accused Canadian ministers and premiers of trying to influence US politics, then partly walked it back; Carney says the claims have "no merit" [^2].

Two dates matter this week. On Wednesday, Oct. 28, the Bank of Canada announces its rate decision: 19 of 34 economists in a Reuters poll expect a rise from 2.25% to 2.50%, its first move in a year, with September inflation at 3.1% [^5]. On Oct. 29 to 30, Carney hosts EU leaders António Costa and Ursula von der Leyen in Montréal, part of his push to trade more with partners other than the US; the government says it wants more chances for young people to live, work and study in Europe [^3].
differences: The US Embassy said Canadian officials were trying to influence US politics; the ambassador later said the embassy "hadn't reached that conclusion," and Carney and Premier Doug Ford deny any interference [^2]. Trump says Canada will give in; Ottawa has not responded [^1].
